item.title: Note 6
item.description:
Notes No. 6
Market order / Limit order. Speed of execution against control of price.
A market order asks to buy or sell at the best price available when it reaches the market. In a liquid market it is usually filled almost at once, but the final price is not known in advance and can differ from the last quote, especially when prices move fast. A limit order sets the worst price acceptable: a maximum to buy, a minimum to sell. It will never fill at a worse price, but it may fill only in part or not at all if the market does not reach that level.
Notes from my trading. Not investment advice.
